Coforge Q2 Net Profit Jumps 56.5% to ₹588 Crore on AI-Led Deal Execution
Coforge Q2 results: Net profit surges 56.5% to ₹588 cr, revenue up 53.6%
items.summary:
Coforge posted a 56.5 per cent increase in consolidated profit to Rs 588 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by AI-led execution of deals, the company said on Friday.
The IT firm had posted a net profit of Rs 375.8 crore in the same period a year ago.
"Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call.
Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter  across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter.
The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent.
Revenue from operations during the reported quarter increased by 53.6 per cent to Rs 6,171 crore from Rs 4,016 crore a year

items.summary: Start your morning with Opening Bell, Moneycontrol’s live pre-market show, as we get you ready for today’s trade. With Wall Street ending higher on a tech-led rally, led by SpaceX’s 7% surge on strong earnings and merger prospects with Tesla, we look at what it means for Indian markets. Brent crude is hovering around $110, US yields remain elevated with the 10-year at 5.12%, and traders are watching the Fed meeting on October 28. We also track Gift Nifty for cues on the opening, along with FII and DII activity after Nifty held the 22,800 mark yesterday and the broader markets came under pressure. All eyes are on the Jio IPO, which was fully subscribed within 100 minutes on day one and drew bids worth ₹3.2 lakh crore, making it India’s largest-ever public issue. We also bring you the key stocks in focus on the back of Q2 earnings from Indian Hotels, KEI Industries and M&M Financial Services, and Persistent Systems’ ₹4,265 crore QIP plan. Watch live for expert views, stock ideas and the levels to track as the market gets ready for the opening bell. Like, share and subscribe to Moneycontrol for the latest market updates.
